overview.title: Bastion of the Angel
overview.p1: A fortified point facing the ocean on the Mazagan ramparts. Climb up for the open horizon and Atlantic trade winds.
overview.p2: Adjacent sections of the ramparts connect easily on foot.
overview.p3: Combine this visit with the Portuguese Cistern during the same morning.

1.desc: Check opening schedules on the morning of your visit.

2.title: Footwear & Wind
2.desc: Stone paths and Atlantic breeze — bring sturdy shoes and a light layer.

food.title: Food nearby
food.p1: Seafood spots and cafés just minutes from the heart of the Portuguese City.
food.p2: Carry water on the walls; sit-down meals are located along the waterfront.

q1.question: Is there an entry fee?
q1.answer: It depends on the area — the cistern requires a ticket; large sections of the ramparts are free to access.

q2.question: How long do I need?
q2.answer: 30 to 90 minutes for most individual stops; half a day for the full Portuguese City core.

q3.question: Best time of day?
q3.answer: Morning for softer light inside the cistern and cooler walks on the ramparts.

q4.question: What to combine it with?
q4.answer: The cistern, ramparts, bastion, and a oceanfront lunch fit perfectly into one loop.

q5.question: Family friendly?
q5.answer: Yes for children comfortable walking; watch out for steep steps along the rampart paths.
